mission: GCRI is a small nonprofit, nonpartisan think tank that studies events that could badly harm or destroy human civilisation — AI, nuclear war, pandemics, climate change and more. It tries to bridge academic research and real-world decision-making in government and industry. It was founded in 2011 by Seth Baum and Tony Barrett.

key_work.title: 2020 Survey of Artificial General Intelligence Projects for Ethics, Risk, and Policy
key_work.plain_summary: Maps the projects around the world explicitly trying to build general AI — who runs them, what they aim for and whether they take safety seriously.

key_work.title: AI Risk, September 2026 (commentary)
key_work.plain_summary: An updated tour of AI risk: argues US military misuse of AI is raising nuclear war risk, while some cyberattack and AI-takeover risks may be overstated.

key_work.title: AI Strategy, September 2026 (commentary)
key_work.plain_summary: Argues AI companies should stop developing and testing new AI systems and the US military should use AI more responsibly, with civic advocacy pushing the federal government to act.

key_work.title: Long-Term Trajectories of Human Civilization
key_work.plain_summary: Compares possible long-run futures — collapse, stagnation, transformation, expansion into space — to show why avoiding catastrophe matters so much.

key_work.title: A Model for the Probability of Nuclear War
key_work.plain_summary: Builds a structured model of the different ways nuclear war could start, as a basis for estimating and reducing its likelihood.

warnings.text: Some events could significantly harm or even destroy human civilization at the global scale.
Military misuse of AI may be raising the risk of nuclear war.
AI development is outpacing governance; companies keep building and testing ever more capable systems.

recommendations.text: AI companies should stop developing and testing new AI systems (GCRI commentary, Sept 2026).
Militaries should use AI more responsibly, especially near nuclear command and control.
Citizens should press their governments through civic advocacy to act on AI risk.
Analyse risks across domains together rather than in silos.
